newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS says traffic growth continued in June.
newsitem.headline: SAS says traffic growth continued in June.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) chief Jan Stenberg said on Thursday that passenger traffic growth continued in June after May's rise but declined to say by how much.
"The positive tendency from March, April and May continued in June," he said at a briefing.
May passenger traffic grew 4.8 percent year-on-year. June figures are due to be published on July 8.

SAS, jointly owned by the governments of Denmark, Norway and Sweden and by private investors, has been under increasing pressure in its home market since deregulation opened the Scandinavian skies to competition.
The carrier logged a loss of 269 million Swedish crowns in the first quarter of 1997, compared to a profit of 311 million in the same period the year before.
One of the factors in the loss was a five percent drop in the number of Euro Class passengers. Stenberg said that Euro Class traffic had since stabilised and that Tourist Class traffic was rising.
